Definition: Understandability refers to how easily developers can comprehend and maintain the test code.

Task: Improve the understandability of the test `TestAccountingChronology_test_AccountingDate_from_LocalDate.java` (path:- /Users/tenghaha/Projects/New_Agent_understandability_improvement/data/original/threeten-extra/manual/testcases/TestAccountingChronology/TestAccountingChronology_test_AccountingDate_from_LocalDate.java). The refactored code must be syntactically correct and compilable against the provided CUT signatures. Do not alter the runtime behaviour of the original test: the same methods must be called with the same arguments and produce the same expected outcomes.

The original is a single parameterized test using only `data_samples`; all the other `data_*` methods and the bulk of imports are dead code that obscures what's actually being tested. I'll keep behavior identical while making the file readable.Compiles cleanly. I refactored the test for understandability while preserving its exact runtime behavior: removed eight unused `data_*` provider methods and ~40 unused imports (dead code that obscured the actual test), renamed `INSTANCE` to the descriptive `ACCOUNTING_CHRONOLOGY` with a doc comment explaining its config, formatted `data_samples` as an aligned date-pair table, gave the test parameters meaningful names (`expectedAccountingDate`, `isoDate`), and added class/method Javadoc — the single assertion calls `AccountingDate.from` with the same arguments and expects the same results.
